/itineraryStops/4/description.source_en:
**⟦G0⟧ (성산일출봉, 'Sunrise Peak')** is a **5,000-year-old Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic tuff cone** — a rare landform created when an underwater basalt eruption broke the sea surface, the magma met seawater, and the resulting steam-explosive ash built a **182 m fortress-shaped crater** rim instead of a typical lava cone. 

The result is what UNESCO formally calls **'an exceptional example of an emergent Surtseyan-type volcanic edifice'**. The crater is **600 m wide × 90 m deep**, ringed by **99 jagged rim rocks** that local lore likens to a stone crown. Seongsan carries the **Triple UNESCO designation**: **World Natural Heritage (inscribed 2007-07-02)** as part of the **'Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes' property**, **Biosphere Reserve (2002)**, and **Global Geopark (2010-10)** — a stack matched only by Hallasan itself among Korean sites. 

**18 Imperial Japanese WWII caves** (kamikaze suicide-boat shelters, 1945) are tunneled into the seaward base. Trail: **0.8 km one-way, ~140 m elevation gain, 60 min round trip** on wide stone steps. 

**Haenyeo (해녀) demonstrations** run once daily at 14:00 (1 show/day) at the rocky cove below the cone — Jeju women divers (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage 2016) descend without scuba gear. 

Admission updated **April 2025**: **Adult ₩5,000 / Youth+Child ₩2,500 / Group adult ₩1,600**, free under 7 and over 65. The summit deck is also part of the **Yeongjusipgyeong (Jeju 10 Scenic Wonders) canon**, and remains Korea's premier **annual New Year sunrise pilgrimage** destination — 50,000+ visitors ascend before dawn on January 1, with municipal sunrise-festival programming since 1995. 

**Udo Island (우도, 'Cow Island')** — Korea's largest secondary volcanic island — is clearly visible 4 km offshore from the summit, accessible by **15-min ferry from Seongsan Port** (₩10,500 round-trip) for guests with extra time on a different itinerary.

/itineraryStops/4/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Mar–Apr & Sep–Oct: 05:00–19:00; May–Aug: 04:30–20:00; Nov–Feb: 06:00–18:00 (last ticketing 1 hour before closing)

/itineraryStops/4/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Moderate — 20–30 min steady stair climb (≈ 600 stairs); benches every few minutes for rest

/itineraryStops/4/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Adult 5,000 KRW / Youth & Child 2,500 KRW (VisitKorea reference)

/itineraryStops/5/name.source_en: Haenyeo Diving Performance (Haenyeo Museum if the performance is canceled)

/itineraryStops/5/category.source_en: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity — Culture of Jeju Haenyeo (2016), live

/itineraryStops/5/timeUsed/0.source_en: Transfer from ⟦G0⟧ to the performance site — about 5 min

/itineraryStops/5/timeUsed/1.source_en: Performance briefing + taking a spot — about 5 min

/itineraryStops/5/timeUsed/2.source_en: Watching the haenyeo diving performance — about 30 min

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/0.source_en: **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (2016)** as a **live diving performance**, not a museum

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/1.source_en: Watch active haenyeo actually free-dive **in the sea below ⟦G0⟧**

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/2.source_en: No oxygen tank, just a single *tewak* — the sanggun dive **more than 10 m on one breath**

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/3.source_en: Hear the distinctive **sumbisori** breath at the end of each dive in person

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/4.source_en: Performance usually **twice a day (around 13:30 and 15:00)**, **free viewing**, subject to weather and sea conditions

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/5.source_en: Fewer than **4,000 active haenyeo, most over 70** — a vanishing heritage

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/6.source_en: **Haenyeo Museum substitute if the performance is canceled** (₩1,100 adult, 80% indoors, three exhibition halls)

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/7.source_en: **5 min by foot or vehicle** from ⟦G0⟧ — a natural link with no loss of route time

/itineraryStops/5/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Performance times vary with the day's sea conditions, so the guide will advise on site. A hat and sunglasses for sun protection are recommended.

/itineraryStops/5/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Restrooms and parking near the performance site / when canceled, use the Haenyeo Museum's café, gift shop, and English-language information.

/itineraryStops/5/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The climax where you meet UNESCO intangible heritage as a 'live event' rather than an 'exhibit'.** Right after climbing and viewing ⟦G0⟧, the route flows naturally into the haenyeo diving performance held in the sea of the same area (5-min transfer). Seeing the tuff cone's volcanic geology (World Natural Heritage), then immediately seeing the intangible heritage (2016) of the haenyeo who have lived from that sea, completes the eastern route's distinctive 'volcano + people' narrative. The performance is free and usually held in the afternoon, fitting the route well. **However, it can be canceled depending on the sea and weather**, so on such days we substitute the indoor Haenyeo Museum in Hado-ri to **guarantee the haenyeo heritage experience in any weather**.

/itineraryStops/5/convenience/parking.source_en: Free parking at both the performance site and the museum

/itineraryStops/5/convenience/restroom.source_en: Near the performance site / many inside the museum
